RS-16 cases in reserve-idempotency.test.js as worded in the Criterion Traceability row, including the second-plan reuse before and after the key purge and the concurrent same-key race
SEC-2 in abuse-limits.test.js with default limits: a second reserve by the same customer -> 409 RESERVATION_LIMIT with no rows; another customer succeeds; the 11th request of a day -> 429

completedWork:
RESERVE (services/reservations.js, route in routes/plans.js): one db.tx = BEGIN IMMEDIATE. Order: key row by (user,key) -> same fingerprint (sha256 of 'POST /api/plans/<id>/reserve\n'+canonical body) replays the stored status and body with Idempotent-Replayed: true, another fingerprint is 422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED; no key row -> reservations by (customer,key): same plan replays the current reservation (200), another plan 422; then plan guards (PLAN_SUPERSEDED, PLAN_NOT_EXECUTABLE, ALREADY_RESERVED, INVALID_STATE, MISSING_BUDGET before MISSING_DEADLINE, PLAN_INVALID via revalidateStoredPlan); then the cap (count of the customer's active reservations >= config.maxLiveReservationsPerCustomer -> 409 RESERVATION_LIMIT details.reservationIds, not stored); then the reservation row, a conditional UPDATE per product (reserved+q<=on_hand) with a reserve ledger row, items, one supplier order (awaiting_supplier) and one created payment operation per supplier (merchant key DEFAULT in single-credential mode), audit, and the stored 201. A withdrawn or replaced offer counts as no stock. OUT_OF_STOCK (details.supplierCodes, newPlanVersionId null) rolls back; a second tx marks the plan non_executable (OUT_OF_STOCK) through the void rule, queues replan_queue and stores the 409; PLAN_*, MISSING_* and OUT_OF_STOCK refusals are stored under the key, RESERVATION_LIMIT, ALREADY_RESERVED, INVALID_STATE and 5xx are not. A UNIQUE violation is caught and re-resolved against what the winner committed. SQLITE_BUSY reaches the app's mapDbError (503 DB_BUSY, Retry-After 1). Refusals are audited as denied. Header Idempotency-Key: missing 400, malformed or repeated 422 VALIDATION_FAILED; a foreign plan is 404 before the header is read.

LEDGER (services/ledger.js): reserveStock, releaseStock, setOnHand (restock/adjust), resetInventory, closeReservation (active->released|expired, one release/expire row per item); one ledger row per change, so SUM(delta) = column holds (asserted in three test files).

VOID RULE (services/void-rule.js): createVoidRule({clock, provider}) returns voidRule(db,{planVersionId, reason, actor, requestId}), run inside the superseding transaction: releases an active reservation (release rows), cancels awaiting_supplier/confirmed orders, marks every non-terminal operation (cancel_requested_at, cancel_reason) and voids created / approved-without-authorize / approved-with-queued-authorize operations locally (queued calls -> cancelled), queues so:<id>:void:1 for authorized ones through provider.queueVoid(db,intent), and leaves authorization_pending, approved with a started or unknown authorize call, and unknown to the protocol. createApp now builds it by default (deps.voidRule) from the clock and createApp({voidProvider}) (default createNoopProvider(), a recorder that sends nothing); createApp({voidRule}) still overrides it.

SUPERSESSION (services/supersession.js): supersedeForOfferChange(ctx,{changes:[{offerId,reason}], drops:[{productId,newOnHand}], actor}) selects proposed/approved versions that use the old offer (json_each over plan_json lines) where the affected supplier's order is not confirmed or later, plus on_hand drops whose planned quantity exceeds on_hand-reserved+own reservation; approved ones get the void rule; each becomes superseded with the reason and the request is queued in replan_queue. markNonExecutable(ctx,{planVersionId,reason,detail,actor}) (approved->non_executable + void rule) and enqueueReplan are shared by refusal, expiry, OUT_OF_STOCK, reset.

SUPPLIER (services/orders.js, routes/supplier.js): list (status filter, 400 on an unknown status), confirm (COMMITMENT_INVALID: unknown/missing/duplicate offer, below planned, after deadline; identical repeat 200; reservation expired 409 RESERVATION_EXPIRED), refuse (order refused, markNonExecutable SUPPLIER_REFUSED with {supplierCode, refusal}, void rule, replan queued, ORDER_EXECUTED after the claim, repeat 200), ready and handover (HANDOVER_BLOCKED unless the plan is executed and no operation is unknown/capture_pending/refund_*, reservation not reconciling; pickup_confirmations row), inventory GET and PATCH (whole-PATCH ownership first: any foreign product 403, then unknown 404; per item a new offer version with the old row replaced, setOnHand with RESERVED_STOCK, supersession in the same tx, response items + superseded ids). Another supplier's order is 404 before the body is read. Refused transitions are audited as denied.

EXPIRY (reservations.js expireDueReservations(ctx,{limit})): CAS active->expired on expires_at<=now, expire rows, plan non_executable (RESERVATION_EXPIRED), void rule; second pass finds nothing; consumed rows never match. The reconciler (e4) calls it.

ADMIN (services/admin.js, routes/admin.js): reset (guard read inside the write tx, 409 RESET_BLOCKED with details.operations; approved plans -> non_executable DEMO_RESET through the void rule; operations and provider_calls archived, never deleted; requests tombstoned (raw_text null, archived_at, images/extractions/replan_queue deleted, originalWording nulled, image files unlinked after commit); catalog restored from the version-1 offers and the seed ledger rows with admin_reset adjust rows; fake_paypal_* tables, fault_flags, request_create and plan:* rate events cleared; own audit row carrying actor and reason; force needs reason 10-500; stranded listed when an operation is not terminal afterwards), faults (stock_depletion withdraws the active offers and supersedes via the same service as the supplier PATCH; supplier_refusal calls refuseSupplierOrder per open order; refund_order; fake_paypal / fake_model flags; clear; FAULTS_UNAVAILABLE with a real adapter; test-only faults need RS_TEST_HOOKS; each audited with actor and target ids), timeline (audit + ledger + provider_call + webhook, time order, requestId filter, afterId/limit paging) and metrics.

TESTS: 81 cases in six files under the net guard, named by criterion (RS-14, RS-15 (part), RS-16, RS-27, RS-28, RS-30, RS-13 offer-change half, RS-17 supplier half, RS-32 admin half, RS-37, SEC-2, SEC-11, F-TR-15), including a held write lock with busy_timeout 0 (server started first, FU-10 style) and key-set comparisons with the contract fixtures.
remainingIssues: 1. CONFLICT WITH A c2 TEST (the full suite is red by exactly this case, ev:ev-mv2r5ewg-01518bd8: 750 tests, 749 pass, 1 fail). test/api/requests-plans.test.js, case 'confirm: an executing or executed plan version is 409 PLAN_IN_PROGRESS; a live reservation without the void rule is refused too' asserts the old fail-closed stopgap: a requirements change over an APPROVED plan holding an ACTIVE reservation is refused 409. With the void rule wired by default (the spec: a requirements change supersedes proposed/approved versions, void rule) that confirm now succeeds (201), supersedes the plan (REQUIREMENTS_CHANGED), releases the reservation with release rows and queues a re-plan. The executing/executed half of that case is unchanged. The file is c2's, outside my globs, so I did not edit it. Fix (c2 rework or the orchestrator): in that case replace the 'live' assertions with status 201, plan status superseded with supersede_reason REQUIREMENTS_CHANGED, reservation released, and keep the 'running' (executing) assertion at 409 PLAN_IN_PROGRESS. The alternative (not wiring the rule by default) would leave refusal, expiry, offer changes and the reset without the rule.

2. Re-plan drains are not done here (f1/e4): supersession, refusal, OUT_OF_STOCK and stock_depletion put the request in replan_queue and the request reads 'replanning'; the customer re-plans with POST /api/requests/:id/plan, which removes the entry. RS-32's replacement journey needs the drain (or that click).

3. Provider voids: only the port exists. With the default no-op recorder an `authorized` operation gets cancel_requested_at and a recorded intent but no provider_calls row. e2 must pass a provider whose queueVoid does INSERT OR IGNORE into provider_calls (key so:<supplierOrderId>:void:1, status intent, started_at NULL) via createApp({voidProvider}) and add the resolution hook and void-result handling; sending is the caller's/reconciler's job. The forced reset (spec steps 1-2: send voids, bounded read-resolve pass) is therefore only partly delivered: it queues through the port, archives, and lists every non-terminal operation in `stranded` and in the audit event.
4. refund_order is minimal: it moves captured -> refund_requested under an executed plan and queues so:<id>:refund:1 (INSERT OR IGNORE, status intent). The saga/reconciler (e4) must send it.

5. Conventions e1/d-phase consumers should follow: fault_flags rows are name '<kind>:<fault>' ('fake_paypal:authorize_denied', 'fake_paypal:lost_response:authorize', 'fake_model:timeout'), value = supplier code or '', remaining = count or NULL (until cleared). metrics reads meta keys reconciler_last_tick_at and reconciler_last_tick_ms (null until e4 writes them).

6. Contract-fixture mismatches (fixtures are c5's; I followed the spec): (a) supplier-order-confirm.json shows canMarkReady true right after confirm with the plan only approved; the brief (state table confirmed->ready: plan executed and no unsettled operation, else HANDOVER_BLOCKED) and this task's criterion make it false until the plan is executed, so the fixture should show false (or an executed-plan variant). (b) plan-reserve.json has no `labels`; the reserve response carries labels (spec Labels convention: seeded prices), as c2's plan responses do. (c) admin-timeline.json shows integer cursors; the cursor is an opaque STRING '<atMs>.<sourceIndex>.<rowId>' (a stable merge key across four tables), so any contract test that types cursor from the fixture must accept a string, or the fixture must change. (d) admin-reset.json is consistent: `stranded` is present only when non-empty. SupplierOrder.commitment {bundles, readyAt, confirmedAt} and RESERVATION_LIMIT details.reservationIds match the fixtures as assumed. Supplier-order and inventory item key sets equal the fixtures' (asserted in supplier-orders.test.js).

7. Spec ambiguity decided: the Conventions say the stored status and body are replayed (so a replay of the first answer is 201 with Idempotent-Replayed: true) while the route table says '201 (new) or 200 (replay)'; I replay the stored status from the key row and answer 200 for the purged-key path (reservation row as guard), as the Conventions word it. If the reviewer wants 200 everywhere, it is one line in resolveExisting/replayStored.

8. The reset's audit row is written directly (not through recordAudit) because recordAudit drops free text and the spec wants the operator's reason recorded; the reason is admin-typed 10-500 characters, never request data.

9. The two-OS-process RS-14 tests belong to c6; reserve is correct for them (check and insert in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE, OUT_OF_STOCK not a lock error); FU-5 regression watch: any 'database is locked' at open in those tests is a regression of src/db/connection.js. The general 300/min per-user limit is still unassigned (c1's open item).
